articles.title: Why AI Matters More Than Iran War in Markets
articles.summary: Global equities have rallied to record levels, fueled by euphoria over artificial intelligence. Investors' risk appetite has held up despite volatility in energy markets caused by the war in Iran.
key_points: AI enthusiasm continues to drive market rallies to record levels
Investors prioritize AI opportunities over geopolitical risks
Markets show resilience despite Iran war volatility

articles.title: There aren't enough rockets for space data centers — Cowboy Space raised $275M to build them
articles.summary: Cowboy Space Corporation raised $275 million in Series B funding to develop rockets specifically for launching space data centers, addressing the shortage of launch capacity for orbital AI infrastructure.
key_points: Cowboy Space raised $275M at $2B valuation led by Index Ventures
Company plans to build proprietary rockets for space data centers
First launch expected before end of 2028
Will compete directly with SpaceX and Blue Origin
Each satellite will generate 1MW power for 800 GPUs

articles.title: AI labs' consulting push defies corporate history
articles.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic are launching consulting ventures with major investors, targeting the $600B AI services market through joint ventures with traditional consulting firms.
key_points: OpenAI secured $4B investment from 19 partners including TPG and Brookfield
Anthropic partnered with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs for $1.5B venture
AI services market projected to reach $600B this year
Historical challenges with joint ventures raise concerns about success

articles.title: Microsoft, Google, xAI security test details deleted from US government website
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department removed details about its agreement with major tech companies to test AI models for security vulnerabilities, raising transparency concerns.
key_points: Commerce Department deleted AI security testing agreement details
Microsoft, Google, and xAI had agreed to share AI models for security reviews
Government aims to identify cyberattack and military misuse threats
Deletion raises transparency questions about AI regulation

articles.title: Tech companies tap debt markets to fund AI and cloud expansion
articles.summary: Major technology companies are increasingly relying on debt markets to fund massive AI infrastructure investments, with combined spending expected to exceed $700B this year.
key_points: Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta planning $700B+ combined AI spending
Companies shifting from cash to debt financing for AI investments
Amazon preparing Swiss franc bond offering and $37-42B bond sale
Oracle plans $45-50B in debt and stock for cloud infrastructure
AI boom entering 'more dangerous phase' with rising infrastructure costs

summary_analysis.market_sentiment: Strongly positive on AI, with massive investments continuing despite geopolitical risks
key_themes: AI spending continues to accelerate across major tech companies
Infrastructure constraints driving innovation (space data centers, proprietary rockets)
Growing government scrutiny of AI security and regulation
New business models emerging in AI consulting and services
